historical_reviews.deepseek: The read-only collection direction is relevant, but tail-only evidence cannot prove no new errors and the AFUEFI/downgrade language belongs to the duplicate row-338 case.

historical_reviews.v3_1: Requires immutable cursors/timestamps or full exports so new errors are distinguished from pre-existing entries without clearing logs; severity alone is insufficient without an expected-event allowlist.

original_test_intent: Verify that controlled power-on, BIOS setup entry and normal exit/reboot complete without hang or crash and generate no unexpected new OS, BMC or SEL error events.
original_method: Bind the exact host/boot, preserve complete pre-event logs and cursors, obtain approval for service-impacting BIOS entry/reboot, observe console and reachability milestones, then collect complete post-event logs and classify only new entries against the approved expected-event policy.
manual_activity: Operator or validated console enters BIOS setup and exits through the approved normal path; owner approves the reboot/service window and expected-event allowlist.
safety_requirements: Bind row 1437, not duplicate downgrade row 338
Do not flash or load an AFU package
Preserve logs and never clear them
Capture full ranges/cursors rather than tail only
Stop on hang, crash, boot loop or lost BMC
Do not label all warnings as failures without policy
agent_execution_scope: Present exact BIOS/reboot plan and obtain approval
Separate expected from unexpected new events
engineer_actions: Perform manual BIOS navigation if needed

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: uptime, dmesg and SEL reads are relevant but the last 40 lines can omit events, no baseline distinguishes old entries, and AFUEFI/downgrade outputs are unrelated and unauthorized. sshpass and host-key bypass are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve complete pre-event log cursors, perform only the approved BIOS-entry/normal-exit reboot, track boot milestones, then collect and correlate every new kernel/journal/BMC/SEL event against the expected-event policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Power-on/BIOS entry, normal reboot/no-hang/no-crash/no-error criteria and 5/5-minute timing are preserved; no flash is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use boot-ID plus monotonic/wall-clock correlation across console, system journal, kernel, BMC event service and SEL, retaining complete before/after cursors and decoded new events.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds causal log boundaries, boot milestones and recovery while removing unrelated firmware operations.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects hangs, boot loops, lost management, new device errors and log gaps that tail snapshots can miss.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Boot normally creates informational/warning events; acceptance needs a project allowlist and cannot be reduced to empty logs.

project_override_considerations: The private SEL script may assist after review, but row 1437 does not authorize the AFUEFI downgrade represented by the duplicate row-338 code variant.
expected_evidence: Pre-event boot ID and full log cursors/exports
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Within row 1437 the BIOS boot and normal reboot/log criteria form a coherent clean-boot event check. The unrelated DeepSeek flash language and duplicate row are reference mismatches, not Master conflicts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The reboot path, log sources, allowlist and recovery are finite inputs. Execution is blocked only if safe reboot/recovery or causal log evidence cannot be established after request.

review_improvement: Eliminates an unsafe unrelated downgrade path and replaces truncated tail output with causally bounded, complete event evidence for the actual BIOS boot/reboot.
independent_technical_reasoning: A claim of 'no error log' requires proving which records are new, not observing a short tail after boot. Boot ID, cursors and synchronized timestamps establish causality without destroying history. Because BIOS entry/reboot is service-impacting and may need manual console navigation, the case is REQUIRES even though log collection is automatable.
